Sit on the pec deck with your back flat against the pad and your feet planted.|Set the handles so your upper arms sit level with your shoulders.|Grab both handles with a light bend in your elbows.|Squeeze your chest to bring the handles together in front of you.|Open your arms back slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.

Put your hands on a bench or a sturdy box, slightly wider than your shoulders.|Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.|Lower your chest to the edge of the bench.|Keep your elbows at about forty-five degrees from your body.|Push back up until your arms are straight.

Kneel on the floor and put your hands under your shoulders.|Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.|Lower your chest towards the floor with your elbows tucked.|Stop when your chest is a fist away from the ground.|Push back up without letting your hips sag.

Get into a push-up position with your hands well outside your shoulders.|Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.|Lower your chest until it is just above the floor.|Let your elbows flare out to the sides.|Push the floor away to return to the top.

Put your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor under your shoulders.|Keep your body straight and your core tight.|Lower your chest towards the floor.|Stop when your upper arms are level with your back.|Press back up until your arms lock out.

Set up in a push-up position with your hands very wide.|Lower yourself towards one hand, bending that elbow and keeping the other arm straight.|Slide your chest across to the other hand, staying low.|Push back up on the far side.|Alternate the side you lower to on every rep.

Start with your hips high and your hands and feet on the floor.|Dive your chest down between your hands as you bend your arms.|Sweep forward and push your chest up towards the ceiling.|Straighten your arms with your hips low and your back arched.|Push your hips back up to the start and repeat.

Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your palms on it.|Set your hands slightly wider than your shoulders at chest height.|Keep your body straight and lean in by bending your elbows.|Bring your chest close to the wall.|Push yourself back until your arms are straight.

Stand with your feet together and your arms straight out to the sides.|Jump your feet apart while you clap your hands in front of your chest.|Open your arms wide again as you jump your feet back together.|Keep your arms at shoulder height the whole time.|Repeat at a steady pace.

Stand in a doorway and put a forearm on the frame.|Set your elbow at about shoulder height.|Step forward with the same-side foot until you feel the stretch.|Keep your chest open and your shoulder down.|Hold, then swap arms and repeat.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms slightly bent.|Exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the handles back and outward, away from your body.|Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand tall holding a weight plate by its sides in front of your thighs.|Keep your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows.|Raise the plate in front of you until it reaches eye level.|Pause at the top without leaning back.|Lower the plate slowly back to your thighs.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outwards.|Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.|Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving the barbell upwards.|As the barbell reaches chest level, pull it upwards with your arm, keeping it close to your body.

Set both pulleys at shoulder height and stand in the middle of the station.|Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left, so the cables cross.|Hold your arms out in front of you with a slight bend in the elbows.|Pull your arms out and back until they line up with your shoulders.|Let your arms come back together in front of you slowly.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your back against the backrest.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and position your hands at shoulder level.|Push the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, but do not lock your elbows.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the handles back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench with back support and a dumbbell in each hand.|Bring the dumbbells up to shoulder height with your palms facing forward.|Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.|Keep your back against the pad throughout.|Lower the dumbbells slowly back to your shoulders.

Stand tall holding a light weight plate or dumbbell in each hand.|Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.|Keep your elbows straight and your shoulders down.|Draw small circles with your hands, slowly making them bigger.|Switch direction halfway through the set.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.|Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and chest up.|Pull the barbell towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the cable handle with an overhand grip.|Keep your back straight and your core engaged.|Raise the cable handle in front of you, keeping your arms straight and your palms facing down.|Continue lifting until your arms are parallel to the floor.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the cable handle back to the starting position.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the machine with your chest against the pad and your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Keep your back straight and your core engaged as you pull the handles towards your chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.|Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the handles back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the smith machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Lift the bar off the rack and position it at shoulder level, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.|Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down to shoulder level.

Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the ground.|Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Lift the barbell off the rack and bring it to shoulder level, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward.|Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder level.

Stand up with a barbell in front of your thighs, hands shoulder-width apart.|Keep your chest tall and your shoulders pulled back.|Pull the bar straight up along your body, leading with your elbows.|Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height, no higher.|Lower the bar slowly back down to your thighs.

Sit in the lateral raise machine with the pads against your outer arms.|Set the seat so the pivot lines up with your shoulders.|Push your arms out and up until they reach shoulder height.|Keep your neck relaxed and your traps out of the movement.|Lower the pads slowly back to your sides.

Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine holder or a corner.|Hold the loaded end at your shoulder with one hand, standing in a split stance.|Brace your core and keep your ribs down.|Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.|Bring the bar back to your shoulder under control.

Start on your hands and feet with your hips pushed up high.|Walk your feet in so your body makes an upside-down V.|Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head towards the floor.|Keep your hips high all the way down.|Press back up until your arms are straight.

Put your feet on a bench and walk your hands back towards it.|Push your hips up so your torso is almost vertical.|Lower the top of your head towards the floor between your hands.|Keep your elbows pointing back and slightly out.|Press up until your arms are locked out.

Kick up into a handstand with your hands shoulder-width apart.|Squeeze your glutes and keep your body in a straight line.|Bend your elbows to lower your head towards the floor.|Stop when the top of your head is just above the ground.|Press back up until your arms are straight.

Walk your feet up a wall until you are upside down with your chest facing it.|Set your hands a bit wider than your shoulders.|Bend your elbows and lower your head towards the floor.|Keep your body tight against the wall.|Press back up to the starting position.

Lie face down with your feet against the base of a wall.|Push up and start walking your feet up the wall.|Walk your hands in towards the wall at the same time.|Go up until your chest is close to the wall.|Reverse the walk back down under control.

Stand or sit up tall with your shoulders relaxed.|Bring one straight arm across your chest.|Hook the other forearm under it and pull it closer.|Keep the shoulder down instead of shrugging it.|Hold the stretch, then change arms.

Anchor the ropes and take an end in each hand.|Step back until the ropes are almost tight and bend your knees.|Sit into a quarter squat with your chest up.|Slam the ropes up and down alternately to make waves.|Keep your core braced and the waves going for the whole set.

Set a pulley high and stand side-on to it with your feet wide.|Grab the handle with both hands above the shoulder nearest the stack.|Keep your arms long and your core braced.|Pull the handle down and across your body towards the opposite knee, turning your hips and back foot.|Return the handle slowly to the top and switch sides after the set.

Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench inside the Smith machine.|Roll the bar over your hips and place a pad under it.|Plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart.|Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.|Squeeze your glutes at the top and lower your hips slowly.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang down by your side.|Keeping your back straight and your core engaged, slowly bend sideways at the waist towards the opposite side of the dumbbell, lowering the weight as far as you comfortably can.|Pause for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.

Attach a rope handle to a high pulley and kneel down facing away from the machine.|Hold the rope handle with both hands and place it behind your head, keeping your elbows out to the sides.|Keeping your hips stationary, flex your waist and crunch your torso down towards your thighs.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.|Hold a weight plate or dumbbell on your chest.|Engage your abs and lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your shoulder blades are off the ground.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Kneel on the floor and hold a barbell with both hands, shoulder-width apart.|Roll the barbell forward, extending your arms and keeping your core engaged.|Continue rolling forward until your body is fully extended and your arms are overhead.|Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the barbell back towards your knees, maintaining control.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie on your back with your arms at your sides and your knees bent.|Lift your feet off the floor until your thighs are vertical.|Curl your hips up off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest.|Pause at the top and squeeze your abs.|Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.|Extend your arms straight out to the sides, parallel to the ground.|Engaging your abs, lift your shoulders off the ground and reach your right hand towards your right heel.|Return to the starting position and repeat on the left side, reaching your left hand towards your left heel.|Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie flat on a decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads.|Place your hands behind your head or across your chest.|Engage your abs and slowly lift your upper body off the bench, curling forward until your torso is perpendicular to the ground.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Hang from a pull-up bar with your arms fully extended and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle.|Engage your core and lift your knees towards your chest, bringing them as close to your elbows as possible.|Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on the ground with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.|Hold a weight or medicine ball with both hands in front of your chest.|Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.|Slowly twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your right side.|Pause for a moment, then twist your torso to the left, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your left side.

Sit on the edge of a bench and hold the sides behind your hips.|Lean back slightly and stretch your legs out in front of you.|Pull your knees towards your chest while bringing your torso forward.|Squeeze your abs when your knees and chest meet.|Extend your legs back out slowly without touching the floor.

Sit on a stability ball with your feet shoulder-width apart and flat on the ground.|Hold a weight in one hand and place your other hand on your hip.|Engage your core and slowly bend sideways towards the weighted side, keeping your back straight.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Get into the captain's chair with your forearms on the pads.|Let your legs hang straight with your back against the pad.|Lift both knees towards your chest without swinging.|Curl your hips up slightly at the top of the rep.|Lower your legs slowly until they hang straight again.

Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head.|Lift your shoulders off the floor and bring your knees up.|Bring one elbow towards the opposite knee as you extend the other leg.|Switch sides in a slow, controlled pedalling motion.|Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders.|Keep your body in a straight line and your core braced.|Drive one knee towards your chest.|Swap legs quickly, as if you were running in place.|Keep your hips low and your shoulders over your hands.

Lie on your back with your arms up and your knees over your hips.|Press your lower back into the floor.|Lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg towards the floor.|Stop just before your back arches and come back to the start.|Alternate sides on every rep.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.|Keep your back flat and your neck in line with your spine.|Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back at the same time.|Hold for a second without letting your hips tilt.|Return to all fours and swap sides.

Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to the machine.|Hold the handle with both hands against your chest.|Step away until the cable pulls you towards the stack.|Press your hands straight out in front of you without twisting.|Bring the handle back to your chest under control.

Kneel on one knee side-on to a cable set at chest height.|Hold the handle with both hands at your sternum.|Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and stay tall.|Press the handle straight out and resist the pull to the side.|Return the handle to your chest without letting your hips turn.

Stand side-on to a cable machine set at chest height.|Hold the handle with both hands and press it straight out.|Lock your arms and keep them level with your sternum.|Resist the cable pulling your torso around.|Hold the position, then swap sides and repeat.

Lie on your back with your arms overhead and your legs straight.|Press your lower back flat into the floor.|Lift your shoulders and legs a few centimetres off the ground.|Keep your ribs down and your body in a shallow banana shape.|Hold the position and breathe steadily.

Get into a hollow body position with your arms overhead.|Keep your lower back glued to the floor and your body tense.|Rock backwards and forwards using your shoulders, not your legs.|Do not let your feet or hands touch the ground.|Keep the rocking small and steady.

Lie flat on your back with your arms stretched overhead.|Keep your legs straight and together.|Lift your arms and legs at the same time to meet over your hips.|Touch your hands to your feet at the top.|Lower back down slowly without touching the floor.

Lie on your back with your hands under your hips.|Lift both legs a few centimetres off the floor.|Press your lower back down into the ground.|Kick your legs up and down in small alternating movements.|Keep your legs straight and your core tight.

Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands by your hips.|Press your lower back into the floor.|Lift both legs until they point at the ceiling.|Lower them slowly without touching the ground.|Stop the descent as soon as your back starts to arch.

Get into a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.|Set your feet a little wider than your hips for balance.|Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.|Keep your hips still, without rocking side to side.|Put the hand down and repeat with the other side.

Start in a high plank with your feet together.|Brace your core and keep your hips level.|Jump both feet out wide.|Jump them straight back together.|Keep a steady rhythm without letting your hips bounce.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.|Tuck your toes and lift your knees a couple of centimetres off the floor.|Keep your back flat and your shoulders over your hands.|Push the floor away and hold the position.|Breathe steadily and do not let your hips rise.

Start in a bear plank with your knees hovering off the floor.|Move an opposite hand and foot forward at the same time.|Keep your hips low and your back flat as you crawl.|Take short steps and stay under control.|Crawl back to where you started.

Stand tall and bend forward to put your hands on the floor.|Walk your hands out until you reach a push-up position.|Hold there for a moment with your core tight.|Walk your feet up towards your hands with your legs as straight as you can.|Stand back up and repeat.

Sit on the floor or between two parallettes with your hands beside your hips.|Push down hard and lift your hips off the ground.|Raise your straight legs until they are level with your hips.|Keep your shoulders pushed down and your chest up.|Hold the L shape for as long as you can.

Get into a side plank on your forearm with your feet stacked.|Line up your elbow under your shoulder.|Lower your hip towards the floor without touching it.|Drive your hip back up until your body is straight again.|Finish the reps on one side before swapping.

Lie on a bench and grab it behind your head with both hands.|Lift your whole body up so you rest only on your upper back.|Keep your body rigid in one straight line.|Lower yourself slowly without bending at the hips.|Stop just above the bench and pull back up.

Start standing with your feet hip-width apart.|Drop into a squat and place both hands on the floor.|Jump your feet back into a plank position.|Jump them straight back in towards your hands.|Stand up tall and go into the next rep.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.|Squat down and plant both hands on the floor.|Thrust both feet back until you are in a plank.|Hold the plank for a beat with your core tight.|Pull your feet back in and stand up.

Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it.|Hold the band with both hands against your sternum.|Step away until the band pulls hard to the side.|Press your hands straight forward without rotating.|Bring them back to your chest and keep your hips still.

Anchor a band high and stand side-on with your feet apart.|Hold the band with both hands above the far shoulder.|Pull it down and across your body towards the opposite hip.|Rotate through your torso and let your back foot pivot.|Return along the same path under control.

Anchor a band behind your head and lie on your back.|Hold the band with straight arms over your chest.|Lift your knees to ninety degrees over your hips.|Lower one leg towards the floor while your arms hold the band.|Swap legs and keep your lower back flat throughout.

Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and the barbell resting on your upper chest, just below your collarbone.|Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, keeping your elbows up and your upper arms parallel to the ground.|Lower your body down into a squat position by bending at the knees and hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up.|Pause for a moment at the bottom of the squat, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand in front of a step or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your sides.|Place your right foot on the step, ensuring your entire foot is on the surface.|Push through your right heel and lift your body up onto the step, bringing your left foot up as well.|Once both feet are on the step, lower your left foot back down to the starting position, keeping your right foot on the step.|Repeat the movement, alternating which foot you step up with each time.

Attach the ankle cuff to your ankle and stand facing the cable machine.|Position yourself far enough away from the machine so that there is tension on the cable.|Place your hands on the machine for support.|Keeping your leg straight, slowly move your leg across your body towards the midline.|Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.|Hold a weight in front of your chest with both hands, or place a barbell across your upper back.|Keeping your chest up and your core engaged, slowly lower your body down by bending at the knees and hips.|Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as you can comfortably go.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Set up a barbell on a squat rack at chest height.|Stand facing away from the rack, with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Bend your knees and lower your body down into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.|Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Lift the barbell off the rack and step back, ensuring your feet are still shoulder-width apart.

Stand in front of the smith machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Place one foot behind you on a bench or step, with your toes pointing forward.|Hold onto the smith machine bar for stability.|Bend your front knee and lower your body down into a lunge position, keeping your back straight.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your front heel to return to the starting position.

Rest a barbell on the front of your shoulders with your hands just outside them.|Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your core braced.|Dip a few centimetres by bending your knees, keeping your chest up.|Drive up through your legs and use that push to press the bar overhead.|Lower the bar back to your shoulders and reset before the next rep.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if sitting on a chair.|Keep your chest up and your back straight.|Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground.|Push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell across your upper back.|Lift one foot off the ground and extend it forward, keeping it parallel to the ground.|Bend your standing leg and lower your body down as if sitting back into a chair, keeping your chest up and your back straight.|Lower yourself until your thigh is parallel to the ground, then push through your heel to return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.|Begin by rapidly moving your feet up and down, as if you were running in place.|Keep your movements quick and light, focusing on staying on the balls of your feet.|Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.|Hold the barbell with a wide grip, positioning it overhead with your arms fully extended.|Engage your core and lower your body down into a squat position, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other.|Place your bottom arm under your head for support.|Squeeze the side of your glutes and lift your top leg as high as you can without rotating your hips or leaning backward.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your leg back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Stand with your feet wide apart and your hands together in front of your chest.|Shift your weight onto one leg and bend that knee, pushing your hips back.|Keep the other leg straight with the foot flat on the floor.|Go down until your thigh is close to parallel with the floor.|Push back to the middle and repeat on the other side.

Lie on your side next to a bench, propped on your forearm with your elbow directly under your shoulder.|Rest the inside of your top leg on the bench, at the knee to make it easier or at the ankle to make it harder, with your bottom leg on the floor under it.|Brace your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.|Press your top leg down into the bench and raise your bottom leg until it touches the underside of the bench.|Lower the bottom leg towards the floor with control, keeping your hips up, and switch sides after the set.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back.|Take a large step forward with one leg, keeping your torso upright.|Lower your body by bending your front knee and hip, while keeping your back leg straight.|Continue lowering until your front thigh is parallel to the ground.|Pause for a moment, then push through your front heel to return to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.|Hold onto a stable object for balance if needed.|Slowly lower your body by bending your knees and leaning back, keeping your torso upright.|Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as far as you can comfortably go.|Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Take a step forward with one foot and place it about two feet in front of the other foot.|Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight.|Continue lowering until your front thigh is parallel to the ground, and your back knee is hovering just above the ground.|Pause for a moment, then push through your front heel to return to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.|Lower your body down into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.|As you come up from the squat, extend your arms overhead, reaching towards the ceiling.|Return to the starting position by lowering your arms and bending your knees to squat down again.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.|Hold the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps or rear delts.|Engage your core and keep your chest up as you lower your body down into a squat, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.|Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Set the safety pins or blocks so the bar rests just below your knees.|Stand close to the bar and grip it just outside your legs.|Brace your core and keep your back flat.|Drive your hips forward to stand up tall with the bar.|Lower the bar back to the pins under control.

Strap the belt around your hips and stand on the platform.|Set your feet shoulder-width apart with your toes slightly out.|Hold the handles and unload the weight from the support.|Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.|Drive through your feet to stand back up tall.

Sit in the machine with the pads on the inside of your knees.|Start with your legs open and your back against the seat.|Squeeze your knees together against the resistance.|Hold for a second when your legs meet.|Let the pads push your knees apart slowly.

Hold the loaded end of a landmine bar against your chest with both hands.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Sit down between your hips, letting the bar guide you.|Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.|Push the floor away to stand back up.

Put a small plate or wedge under both heels.|Hold a dumbbell against your chest with both hands.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart on the wedge.|Squat straight down, keeping your torso upright.|Push through your feet to stand back up.

Put your front foot on a low step and your back foot on the floor.|Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.|Keep your torso upright and your weight on the front leg.|Lower your back knee towards the floor.|Push through the front foot to stand back up.

Set the smith machine bar on your upper back and rest one foot on a bench behind you.|Place the front foot far enough forward to keep the knee stacked over the ankle.|Unrack the bar and brace your core.|Lower straight down until your back knee is close to the floor.|Drive through the front heel to return to the top.

Rest the smith machine bar across your upper back and unrack it.|Stand with your feet under the bar and your chest up.|Step one foot back and lower that knee towards the floor.|Keep most of your weight on the front leg.|Push off the front foot to bring your legs back together.

Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.|Step one foot straight back, landing on the ball of the foot.|Lower your back knee until it almost touches the floor.|Keep your front shin vertical and your chest up.|Push through the front heel to step back together.

Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand.|Take a wide step out to one side.|Push your hips back and bend that knee while the other leg stays straight.|Keep both feet flat and your chest up.|Push off the bent leg to return to the middle.

Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet a step forward.|Slide down until your knees are bent at ninety degrees.|Keep your knees over your ankles and your back on the wall.|Rest your hands on your thighs or hold them out in front.|Hold the position until your legs give in.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Squat down and put your hands on the floor.|Jump your feet back into a push-up position and lower your chest.|Push up and jump your feet back under your hips.|Jump straight up with your arms overhead.

Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.|Run on the spot, driving one knee up at a time.|Bring each knee up to hip height.|Land softly on the balls of your feet.|Pump your arms in time with your legs.

Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.|Jump your feet out wide while you raise your arms overhead.|Land softly with your knees slightly bent.|Jump back to bring your feet together and your arms down.|Keep a steady rhythm for the whole set.

Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee.|Jump sideways and land on the other foot.|Swing the free leg behind you as you land.|Absorb the landing softly and stay balanced.|Jump back to the other side and keep alternating.

Get into an athletic stance with your knees bent and your chest up.|Push off one foot to slide sideways.|Take quick steps without crossing your feet.|Stay low and keep your weight on the balls of your feet.|Shuffle back in the other direction.

Start standing with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Drop your hands to the floor and kick your legs back hard.|Let your hips sink towards the ground as you land.|Push back up and pull your feet under your hips.|Stand up and go straight into the next rep.

Stand on one leg with the other leg held out in front of you.|Stretch your arms forward for balance.|Sit down slowly on the standing leg, keeping the free leg off the floor.|Go all the way down until your hamstring meets your calf.|Drive through the whole foot to stand back up.

Hold onto a post or a suspension strap in front of you.|Stand on one leg and lift the other leg forward.|Use your hands to control the descent as you squat down.|Go as low as you can while keeping the free leg up.|Pull lightly on the support and push through your foot to stand.

Stand on one leg and bend the other knee so the foot points back.|Hold that foot behind you with the same-side hand.|Lower yourself until the back knee touches the floor.|Keep your chest up and your standing heel down.|Push back up without letting the back foot touch down.

Stand on one leg with the other leg bent behind you.|Reach your arms forward as a counterweight.|Hinge and squat down until the back knee taps the floor.|Keep your back flat and your standing foot planted.|Stand back up by driving through your heel.

Stand on one leg in front of a box or a bench.|Hold the free leg out in front of you.|Sit back slowly until your glutes touch the box.|Do not drop or bounce off the surface.|Push through the standing foot to come back up.

Loop a band above your knees and stand shoulder-width apart.|Push your knees out so the band stays tight.|Sit back and down into a squat.|Keep your chest up and your knees tracking over your toes.|Drive through your feet to stand back up.

Stand tall and hold a wall with one hand if you need balance.|Bend one knee and grab that ankle behind you.|Pull your heel towards your glute.|Keep your knees together and your hips tucked under.|Hold, then swap to the other leg.

Step onto the treadmill and clip the safety key to your clothes.|Start the belt slowly and find your footing before speeding up.|Raise the speed until you are running at a pace you can hold.|Keep your torso tall and let your arms swing at your sides.|Slow the belt down for a few minutes before you step off.

Step onto the treadmill and set a comfortable walking speed.|Stand tall and look ahead instead of down at your feet.|Let your arms swing naturally rather than gripping the handrails.|Roll through each step from heel to toe.|Slow the belt down before stepping off the machine.

Set the treadmill to a brisk walking speed.|Raise the incline until your legs feel the climb.|Stand tall and avoid leaning on the handrails.|Push through the whole foot on every step.|Drop the incline and the speed to cool down at the end.

Step onto the climber and take a handle in each hand.|Put one foot on each pedal with your body upright.|Drive one knee up as the other leg extends down.|Keep the movement steady instead of bouncing.|Slow the pace down for the last minute of the set.

Set the saddle so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom.|Sit down and put the balls of your feet on the pedals.|Hold the bars with relaxed arms and a flat back.|Pedal at a steady cadence and adjust the resistance to taste.|Spin easy for a couple of minutes to finish.

Sit on the air bike and set the saddle to hip height.|Grab the moving handles and put your feet on the pedals.|Push and pull with your arms while your legs drive the pedals.|Keep your breathing under control as the fan gets louder.|Ease off gradually instead of stopping dead.

Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles.|Stand tall with your weight through the middle of your feet.|Push the pedals around in a smooth oval path.|Work the arms and legs together instead of just coasting.|Lower the resistance for the final minutes.

Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso and arms fully extended.|Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale and slowly begin to lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.|Let the barbell hang at arm's length in front of your thighs.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the barbell up towards your chest by contracting your biceps.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.|Rest your upper arms on the pad of the preacher bench, allowing your arms to fully extend.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the dumbbell in your right hand as you contract your biceps.|Continue to curl the dumbbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.|Pause for a moment, then inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.

Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the cable attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing up.|Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary.|Exhale and curl the cable attachment towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.|Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.

Set up an incline bench at a 45-degree angle.|Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach resting against it.|Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, allowing the barbell to hang down towards the floor.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.

column2: Dumbbell Alternating Bicep Curl with Leg Raised on Exercise Ball
column9: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.|Place an exercise ball behind you and position one foot on top of it, keeping your balance.|With your arms fully extended and elbows close to your sides, curl one dumbbell towards your shoulder while keeping your upper arm stationary.|Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position and repeat with the other arm.|Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.|Hold the cable rope attachment with an underhand grip, palms facing each other, and your arms fully extended.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the cable rope attachment until your biceps are fully contracted and the rope is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing down.|Keep your upper arms stationary and exhale as you curl the barbell upward, contracting your biceps.|Continue to raise the barbell until your biceps are fully contracted and the barbell is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position, keeping your upper arms stationary.

column2: Dumbbell Alternating Seated Bicep Curl on Exercise Ball
column9: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.|Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl one dumbbell while rotating your forearm until your palm is facing your shoulder.|Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.|Repeat the curl with the other arm.

Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.|Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the bar up towards your shoulders.

Attach a straight bar to a low pulley cable machine.|Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the bar towards your chest by contracting your biceps.

Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.|Rest your upper arms against your inner thighs, just above your knees, and let the barbell hang down in front of you.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders, contracting your biceps.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause, then inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

column2: Dumbbell Bicep Curl on Exercise Ball with Leg Raised
column9: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the ground and your back straight.|Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms fully extended.|Slowly curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.|While performing the bicep curl, raise one leg off the ground and hold it in the air for the duration of the exercise.

Stand up straight with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands close together.|Keep your elbows close to your torso and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.|Exhale as you curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Continue to raise the bar until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.|Hold the contracted position for a brief pause as you squeeze your biceps.|Inhale as you slowly begin to bring the barbell back to the starting position.

Set a bench to about 60 degrees and sit back against it.|Let both arms hang straight down with a dumbbell in each hand.|Curl the dumbbells up without letting your elbows drift forward.|Squeeze your biceps at the top of the curl.|Lower the weights slowly until your arms are fully straight.

Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your back pressed against the bench.|Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.|Unrack the barbell and lower it slowly towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.|Pause for a moment when the barbell touches your chest.|Push the barbell back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

Sit on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs.|Using your thighs to help raise the dumbbells, lift the dumbbells one at a time so that you can hold them in front of you at shoulder width.|Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position.|As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells to your side until they are about level with your chest.|As you exhale, use your triceps to lift the dumbbells back to the starting position. Make sure to use only your triceps and do not use your forearms or biceps to help lift the dumbbells.

Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.|Slide your butt off the bench and straighten your legs in front of you, keeping your heels on the ground.|Bend your elbows and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your back close to the bench.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push yourself back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench with your hands gripping the edge, fingers pointing forward.|Slide your butt off the bench, supporting your weight with your hands.|Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.|Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

column2: Barbell Decline Close Grip to Skull Press
column9: Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet and hold a barbell with a close grip.|Lower the barbell towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.|Pause for a moment, then extend your arms to press the barbell back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on a bench or chair with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.|Hold the cable handle with your right hand and place your elbow on the inside of your right knee.|Extend your arm fully, keeping your elbow stationary and close to your knee.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your arm back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.|Rest your upper arms on the pad and grab the handles.|Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad.|Push the handles down until your arms are straight.|Let the handles come back up slowly until your elbows are fully bent.

Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the bench with your feet flat on the ground.|Grasp the barbell with a close grip, slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.|Lower the barbell towards your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push the barbell back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with your hands gripping the edge next to your hips.|Slide your butt off the front of the bench with your legs extended in front of you.|Keep your back close to the bench and your elbows slightly bent.|Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.|Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.

Lie on a decline bench with your head lower than your feet and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.|Extend your arms fully, keeping your elbows close to your head.|Lower the dumbbells slowly behind your head, bending your elbows.|Pause for a moment, then raise the dumbbells back to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Adjust the cable machine to a low pulley position.|Attach a straight bar to the cable.|Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and extend your arms straight overhead.|Lean forward slightly, keeping your back straight and core engaged.

Lie on a flat bench and hold the bar with a grip just narrower than your shoulders.|Press the bar up over your chest with your arms straight.|Bend your elbows and let the bar travel down towards your chin, keeping your elbows pointing forward.|Stop a few centimetres above your throat.|Press the bar back up by straightening your arms.

Put one knee and the same-side hand on a bench with your back flat.|Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with your upper arm tucked against your side.|Start with your elbow bent to 90 degrees.|Straighten your arm behind you until it is fully extended.|Bend the elbow slowly back to 90 degrees and switch arms after the set.

Start in a high plank position with your hands placed close together, directly under your shoulders.|Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground, keeping your elbows close to your sides.|Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

column2: Barbell Lying Back of the Head Tricep Extension
column9: Lie flat on a bench with your feet flat on the ground and your head at the end of the bench.|Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and extend your arms straight up over your chest.|Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows.|Pause for a moment, then extend your arms back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Attach a rope to a high pulley and take an end in each hand.|Stand tall with your elbows pinned to your sides.|Push the rope down until your arms are straight.|Spread the ends of the rope apart at the bottom and squeeze your triceps.|Let the rope rise back to chest height without moving your elbows.

Lie back on a bench holding one dumbbell with both hands.|Press the dumbbell up until your arms are straight over your chest.|Keep your upper arms still and bend only at the elbows.|Lower the dumbbell behind your head until you feel the triceps stretch.|Extend your arms back to the top without flaring your elbows.

Hold a dumbbell in one hand and press it straight overhead.|Keep your upper arm next to your ear and your elbow pointing up.|Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending the elbow.|Go down until your forearm touches your biceps.|Extend your arm back overhead and squeeze the triceps.

Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair and grip the front with both hands.|Slide your hips off the seat with your legs out in front.|Bend your elbows to lower your hips towards the floor.|Stop when your upper arms are level with the seat.|Push back up until your arms are straight.

Sit on the floor with your hands behind you and your knees bent.|Lift your hips so only your hands and feet touch the ground.|Walk forward by moving an opposite hand and foot together.|Keep your hips up the whole time.|Walk back the other way to finish the set.

Place a dumbbell on the ground in front of a bench.|Stand facing away from the bench with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Bend at the knees and hips to lower yourself down towards the bench, keeping your chest up and back straight.|Once your glutes touch the bench, push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.|Place the barbell across your upper back, resting it on your traps.|Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight.|Lower your torso until it is parallel to the ground, feeling a stretch in your hamstrings.|Engage your glutes and hamstrings to raise your torso back up to the starting position.

Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes pointing slightly outward.|Hold a weight in front of your chest with both hands.|Shift your weight to one side and lower your body by bending the knee of the side you shifted towards, while keeping the other leg straight.|Go as low as you can while maintaining balance and keeping your chest up.|Push through the heel of the bent leg to return to the starting position.

Attach a cable to a low pulley and stand facing away from the machine.|Place the cable around your ankle and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Keep your core engaged and your back straight throughout the exercise.|Slowly extend your leg straight back, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.|Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.

Set the Smith bar at mid-thigh height and grip it just outside your legs.|Unlock the bar and stand tall with a soft bend in your knees.|Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs with a flat back.|Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.|Drive your hips forward to stand back up.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms by your sides.|Bend forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent.|Reach down towards your toes with your hands, keeping your legs as straight as possible.|Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.|Take a step forward with your right foot, keeping your back straight and core engaged.|Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.|Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.|Repeat with your left leg.

Sit on a bench with your back against the bench and your feet flat on the ground.|Place your hands on the bench for support.|Engage your glutes and hamstrings, then lift your hips off the bench until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.|Hold the barbell in the crooks of your elbows, with your hands gripping the barbell for stability.|Engage your core and keep your chest lifted as you lower your hips back and down into a squat position.|Keep your knees in line with your toes and your weight in your heels.|Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.|Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat.|Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down your legs.|Stop when you feel a stretch along the back of your thighs.|Squeeze your glutes to bring your hips forward and stand tall.

Set up the smith machine with the barbell at shoulder height.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.|Step under the bar and position it across your upper back, resting on your traps.|Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Unrack the bar and take a step back, maintaining a stable stance.

Adjust the barbell on the smith machine to an appropriate height for your body.|Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed outwards.|Position yourself under the barbell, resting it on your upper traps and shoulders.|Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.|Engage your core and keep your chest up as you unrack the barbell.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.|Jump up explosively, extending your hips, knees, and ankles.|While in mid-air, quickly bring your feet together.|Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately drop back into a squat position.

Start by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your toes slightly turned out.|Hold the barbell behind your legs, resting it on your upper thighs.|Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, keeping your back straight and your chest up.|Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.|Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.

Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell over your hips.|Plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart and under your knees.|Tuck your chin and drive through your heels to lift your hips.|Squeeze your glutes hard when your body forms a straight line.|Lower your hips slowly until they nearly touch the floor.

Sit with your upper back on a bench and a dumbbell resting on your hips.|Hold the dumbbell in place with both hands.|Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body is level.|Squeeze your glutes at the top for a second.|Lower your hips under control without dropping them onto the floor.

Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.|Rest your arms at your sides with your palms down.|Push through your heels to lift your hips off the floor.|Squeeze your glutes until your body forms a straight line.|Lower your hips back down slowly, one vertebra at a time.

Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor.|Lift the other leg and hold it straight in the air.|Push through the planted heel to raise your hips.|Keep your hips level, without letting one side drop.|Lower yourself slowly and finish all the reps before swapping legs.

Lie on your back with your knees bent and a dumbbell across your hips.|Hold the dumbbell steady with both hands.|Drive your heels into the floor and lift your hips.|Pause at the top with your glutes squeezed tight.|Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

Lie on your back and lift your hips into a bridge position.|Hold your hips level and your ribs down.|Bring one knee up towards your chest without dropping your hips.|Put that foot back down and repeat with the other leg.|Keep alternating legs while you hold the bridge.

Stand inside a trap bar with your feet hip-width apart.|Push your hips back and grab both handles with straight arms.|Lift your chest and take the slack out of the bar.|Drive your feet into the floor and stand up tall.|Push your hips back to lower the bar to the floor.

Sit in the machine with the pads against the outside of your knees.|Keep your back flat against the seat and hold the handles.|Push your knees apart as far as the machine allows.|Squeeze your glutes for a moment at the widest point.|Bring your knees back together slowly.

Stand facing the machine and put one foot on the lever pad.|Hold the chest support and keep your back flat.|Push the pad back and up with your working leg.|Squeeze the glute at the end of the push.|Return the pad slowly and do all the reps on that side first.

Strap a cable cuff around the ankle furthest from the machine.|Hold the frame for balance and stand tall.|Lift the working leg out to the side, keeping it straight.|Stop when you feel the side of your glute working.|Bring the leg back down slowly without letting the stack rest.

Lie face down on the machine with your hips at the edge of the pad.|Hold the handles and let your legs hang down.|Squeeze your glutes to lift your legs until they are level with your back.|Avoid arching your lower back at the top.|Lower your legs slowly and do not let them swing.

Stand with your feet wide and your toes turned out.|Hold one dumbbell with both hands between your legs.|Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower the weight.|Keep your chest up and the dumbbell close to your body.|Drive through your heels to stand up and squeeze your glutes.

Take a wide stance with your toes pointing out.|Hold a dumbbell hanging between your legs with both hands.|Keep your chest up and your back straight.|Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.|Push through your heels and squeeze your glutes on the way up.

Stand on a low platform with a dumbbell in each hand.|Step one foot back and off the platform.|Lower your back knee towards the floor, below the level of the front foot.|Keep your torso upright and your front heel planted.|Drive up through the front leg to return onto the platform.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand.|Step one foot back and across behind the other leg.|Bend both knees to lower into the curtsy position.|Keep your hips facing forward and your chest up.|Push through the front heel to stand back up.

Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.|Step one foot back and diagonally behind the other.|Bend both knees to sink into the lunge.|Keep your hips square and your front knee over your foot.|Push through the front heel to return to standing.

Lie on your back and put the soles of your feet together.|Let your knees fall out to the sides.|Pull your heels in close to your body.|Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.|Lower your hips slowly and repeat without resting.

Get on all fours with your hands under your shoulders.|Keep your back flat and your core braced.|Push one heel up towards the ceiling with the knee still bent.|Stop when your thigh is level with your body.|Lower the knee back down without touching the floor.

Start on all fours with your knees under your hips.|Keep your knee bent at ninety degrees.|Lift that leg out to the side, away from your body.|Stop before your torso starts to lean over.|Lower the knee back down under control.

Lie on your side with your knees bent and your feet stacked.|Rest your head on your bottom arm and keep your hips still.|Open the top knee towards the ceiling, keeping your feet together.|Stop before your hips start to roll back.|Close the knee slowly and repeat.

Stand on one leg and hinge forward with the other leg back.|Reach your arms out to the sides for balance.|Rotate your hips open towards the ceiling.|Rotate them back the other way until they face the floor.|Move slowly and keep the standing knee soft.

Lie on your side with your legs stacked and straight.|Support your head with your bottom arm.|Lift the top leg towards the ceiling.|Keep your toes pointing forward, not up.|Lower the leg slowly without letting it rest.

Loop a short band just above your knees.|Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat.|Push your knees out against the band.|Drive through your heels to lift your hips.|Squeeze your glutes at the top and lower slowly.

Sit with your upper back on a bench and a band around your hips.|Anchor both ends of the band under your feet or to the rack.|Push your hips up against the band's pull.|Squeeze your glutes when your body is level.|Lower your hips slowly without losing the tension.

Loop a band above your knees and lie on your back.|Put the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open.|Press your knees out against the band.|Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.|Lower under control and go straight into the next rep.

Loop a band above your knees and lie on your side.|Bend your knees and stack your feet.|Open the top knee against the band without rolling your hips.|Hold for a second at the top.|Close the knee slowly and keep the tension.

Put a band around your legs, just above the knees or at the ankles.|Bend your knees slightly and push them out against the band.|Step sideways without letting your feet come together.|Take several steps in one direction.|Walk back the other way to finish the set.

Loop a band around your ankles and get into a quarter squat.|Keep tension on the band by pushing your knees out.|Step forward and out at a diagonal with one foot.|Repeat with the other foot, staying low.|Walk forwards, then walk backwards the same way.

Loop a band around one foot and hold the other end under your hands.|Get on all fours with your back flat.|Push the banded foot up towards the ceiling with the knee bent.|Squeeze the glute at the top of the kick.|Bring the knee back down slowly against the band.

Loop a band above your knees and get on all fours.|Keep your hips level and your back flat.|Lift one knee out to the side against the band.|Do not let your torso lean to the other side.|Lower the knee slowly and keep the band under tension.

Anchor a band low and loop the free end around one ankle.|Stand facing the anchor and hold something for balance.|Kick the banded leg straight back, keeping it long.|Squeeze your glute at the end of the kick.|Bring the leg forward slowly against the band.

Loop a band around both ankles and stand tall.|Hold a wall or a rack for balance.|Lift one leg straight out to the side against the band.|Keep your torso upright and your hips square.|Bring the leg back in slowly and repeat.

Sit on a bench with a band looped above your knees.|Plant your feet and keep your back straight.|Push your knees apart against the band.|Hold the open position for a second.|Let your knees come back together slowly.

Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front of you.|Tuck your hips under so your lower back flattens.|Push your hips forward until you feel the front of the back thigh stretch.|Keep your chest tall and your shoulders relaxed.|Hold, then swap sides.

Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together.|Pull your heels in towards your body.|Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall.|Let your knees fall out towards the floor.|Lean forward gently and hold the stretch.

Step onto the stair machine and start it at a slow speed.|Stand upright and rest your hands lightly on the rails.|Take full steps instead of short, bouncy ones.|Push through your heel on every step to use the glutes.|Drop the speed before you step off.

Adjust the seat of the leg press machine so that your knees are slightly bent when your feet are on the footplate.|Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your feet flat on the footplate, shoulder-width apart.|Place your toes and the balls of your feet on the footplate, keeping your heels off the edge.|Release the safety handles and push the footplate away from you by extending your knees.|Once your knees are fully extended, slowly lower your heels by flexing your calves.

Stand on a raised platform with your toes on the edge and your heels hanging off.|Hold onto a stable object for support.|Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Adjust the machine to your height and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.|Place your shoulders under the pads and hold onto the handles for stability.|Raise your heels as high as possible by extending your ankles.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.|Place your hands on a wall or stable surface for balance.|Slowly raise your heels off the ground, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

column2: Barbell Standing Rocking Leg Calf Raise
column9: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell across your upper back.|Raise your heels off the ground as high as possible, balancing on the balls of your feet.|Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Stand on a low box or step on one leg.|Let the other leg hang just off the edge.|Bend your standing knee slowly to lower the free heel towards the floor.|Tap the floor lightly without shifting your weight onto it.|Straighten your standing leg to rise back up and switch legs after the set.

column2: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise
column9: Sit on a bench with the ball of one foot on a low step and your heel hanging off.|Rest a dumbbell on top of that knee and hold it in place.|Push through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as you can.|Pause at the top and squeeze your calf.|Lower your heel slowly below the step and switch legs after the set.

Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and step under it.|Rest the bar across your upper back and stand with the balls of your feet on a low step.|Unlock the bar and let your heels hang off the edge.|Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.|Lower your heels slowly below the step.

Stand with your toes on an elevated surface, such as a step or block.|Place your hands on a stable support, such as a wall or railing, for balance.|Raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body weight onto the balls of your feet.|Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.|Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
